title: AI infrastructure value chain
map_limitation: Supplier-side search cannot surface diversified suppliers that name no customer; such names enter via research and the repricing-lag lane. Seed heat scores are analyst-authored [INFERRED]; first `run heat` refresh replaces them with fetched PCS data.

links.name: AI applications & agents
links.role: Consumer- and enterprise-facing software where AI demand originates; monetization layer that justifies everything upstream.

bottleneck.note: Abundant supply of applications; the constraint is distribution, not capacity.

impact.rationale: Demand origin, but value spread across thousands of players; the occurrence lifts the category more than any single name.

evidence.claim: App-layer AI revenue is growing but fragmented across incumbents' suites rather than concentrated.

crowdedness.rationale: The default retail AI exposure alongside chips; heavily narrated.

evidence.claim: App-layer AI names are staples of retail AI coverage and thematic ETFs.

capture.rationale: Moats unclear at the app layer; model commoditization pressures pricing.

evidence.claim: Fast follower dynamics and open-weight models compress app-layer differentiation.

repricing_check.note: Not run; heterogeneous layer, run per-name at screen stage.

links.name: Frontier model labs
links.role: Train and serve the frontier models the application layer consumes; the largest single buyers of compute.

bottleneck.note: A handful of labs set the compute demand curve; private (OpenAI, Anthropic) or embedded in megacaps.

impact.rationale: Their scaling decisions are the demand signal for the entire chain.

evidence.claim: Frontier lab compute commitments anchor hyperscaler capex plans.
evidence.source_name: capex guidance and disclosed compute deals

crowdedness.rationale: Maximum narrative saturation; every valuation and funding round is front-page.

evidence.claim: Frontier lab funding rounds receive blanket mainstream coverage.

capture.rationale: Enormous value creation, contested capture: training costs, price competition, and open-weight pressure.

evidence.claim: Inference price declines through 2025-26 despite capability gains.

links.name: AI data centers
links.role: The physical buildout: hyperscaler and neocloud campuses that house accelerators; where capex turns into orders for every upstream link.

bottleneck.note: Powered-shell capacity is scarce; time-to-power now gates deployments more than chip supply.

impact.rationale: Direct recipient of the capex wave; backlog visibility in REIT/neocloud disclosures.

evidence.claim: Record data-center leasing and pre-leasing disclosed through 2025-26.

crowdedness.rationale: Well-covered by both institutions and retail since 2024; neoclouds heavily narrated.

evidence.claim: Data-center trade is a named retail theme with dedicated ETFs.

capture.rationale: Capital-intensive, tenant concentration, financing sensitivity; spreads competed.

evidence.claim: Development yields compressed as capital chased the theme.

links.name: AI accelerators (GPUs/XPUs)
links.role: The compute engines; the most visible link in the chain and its largest dollar pool.

bottleneck.note: Single-vendor concentration at the top; supply improving but allocation still strategic.

impact.rationale: The chain's revenue epicenter; every buildout dollar passes through this link first.

evidence.claim: Accelerator revenue is the largest and fastest-growing line of the buildout.

crowdedness.rationale: The single most-owned and most-discussed trade in retail markets; Ron's own reference case for CROWDED.

evidence.claim: Top of retail attention rankings continuously since 2023.

capture.rationale: Extraordinary pricing power and ecosystem lock-in at the leader.

evidence.claim: Sustained premium margins through the cycle at the category leader.

repricing_check.note: The 'is it really there' test: consensus estimates rose in step with price through 2024-26, so the move is numbers-backed, not story-only. Crowded AND repriced; not a repricing-lag candidate. Residual question is durability of the capex cycle (see scenarios), not discovery.

links.name: High-bandwidth memory
links.role: HBM stacks co-packaged with accelerators; capacity contracted years ahead by a three-player oligopoly.

bottleneck.note: HBM supply sold out into forward years; qualification cycles lock sockets.

impact.rationale: Content per accelerator rising generation over generation; direct beneficiary of every unit shipped.

evidence.claim: HBM bit demand growth outpaces overall DRAM as AI content per package rises.

crowdedness.rationale: Fully discovered as 'the other AI trade' since 2024; Ron's second reference case.

evidence.claim: Memory names feature persistently in retail AI coverage.

capture.rationale: Oligopoly with qualification lock-in, but memory remains cyclical with capex-driven busts.

evidence.claim: Three suppliers control HBM; pricing strong in upcycle, historically mean-reverting.

repricing_check.note: Partially repriced: estimates up strongly but valuation vs own history mid-range; watch for cycle-peak signals rather than discovery gap.

links.name: Advanced packaging
links.role: CoWoS-class 2.5D/3D packaging that marries logic dies to HBM; a genuine physical chokepoint of the buildout.

bottleneck.note: Packaging capacity, not wafer starts, has repeatedly gated accelerator output.

impact.rationale: Named repeatedly as the gating step for accelerator shipments; capacity expansions pre-sold.

evidence.claim: Packaging capacity called the binding constraint on AI chip output in multiple periods.

crowdedness.rationale: Known to semis specialists, thin in retail attention; mostly wrapped inside TSMC exposure.

evidence.claim: OSAT names carry a fraction of the attention of the chip designers they package.

capture.rationale: Leader captures well; merchant OSATs more competed; equipment niche (hybrid bonding) concentrated.

evidence.claim: Packaging equipment for hybrid bonding is a near-duopoly niche.

links.name: Leading-edge foundry
links.role: Fabricates every accelerator die; the deepest moat in the chain.

bottleneck.note: Effectively one supplier at the leading edge; geopolitical single point of failure.

impact.rationale: Every AI die passes through; pricing power rising with each node.

evidence.claim: Leading-edge wafer pricing and AI revenue share climbing.

crowdedness.rationale: Institutionally a consensus holding and retail-visible, though less feverish than designers.

evidence.claim: Foundry leader is a top holding across global funds and a frequent retail mention.

capture.rationale: Near-monopoly at the edge with proven pricing power.

evidence.claim: Sustained structural margin premium at the leading-edge leader.

repricing_check.note: Not yet run; valuation vs own history is the interesting leg here.

links.name: Networking & optics
links.role: Scale-out and scale-up fabric: switches, optical transceivers, co-packaged optics, and the fiber plant between AI pods and campuses.

bottleneck.note: 800G/1.6T transitions strain transceiver and cable supply in bursts.

impact.rationale: Networking content per GPU rising; optics upgrade cycle attached to every cluster generation.

evidence.claim: Networking share of AI cluster BOM increases with cluster scale.

crowdedness.rationale: Optics discovered hard in 2025-26 (large re-ratings); no longer dark, not yet GPU-level.

evidence.claim: Optical transceiver names re-rated sharply on AI orders through 2025-26.

capture.rationale: Fast innovation cycles and customer concentration; periodic price-downs between generations.

evidence.claim: Transceiver ASPs decline within generations; share shifts between cycles.

repricing_check.note: Run per-name; several optics names may be crowded AND repriced already.

links.name: Thermal & liquid cooling
links.role: Direct-to-chip and immersion cooling plus thermal management; mandatory at modern rack densities, attached to every new AI hall.

bottleneck.note: Not scarce, but spec'd-in early; water availability is the quieter constraint alongside it.

impact.rationale: Rack densities force liquid cooling adoption; content per MW rising.

evidence.claim: Liquid cooling moved from optional to required at current accelerator TDPs.

crowdedness.rationale: Lead names discovered in 2024-25; second-tier and component suppliers much less so.

evidence.claim: Category leader widely covered; component chain thinly followed.

capture.rationale: Real engineering content but rising competition from industrial incumbents; risk of commoditization at the component layer.

evidence.claim: Multiple industrial entrants announced cooling lines 2025-26.

links.name: Power equipment
links.role: Transformers, switchgear, UPS, busway, and backup generation that electrify data centers and the grid segments feeding them.

bottleneck.note: Large power transformer lead times stretched to multiple years; installed base replacement compounds AI demand.

impact.rationale: Every MW of AI capacity buys transformers, switchgear, and backup; demand also stacked on grid replacement and electrification.

evidence.claim: Multi-year backlogs and record orders reported across electrical equipment makers.

crowdedness.rationale: Institutionally recognized, but retail attention remains a fraction of chip-layer links; rarely narrated as an AI trade.

evidence.claim: Electrical equipment names near-absent from retail AI discussions relative to semis.

capture.rationale: Concentrated supply, long qualification, price escalators in backlog; genuine pricing power this cycle.

evidence.claim: Price/mix cited as a margin driver across the group; lead times support pricing.

links.name: Grid & interconnection
links.role: Transmission buildout, substations, and the interconnection process itself; the queue that decides when data centers get power.

bottleneck.note: Interconnection queues and transmission siting are the slowest step in the entire chain.

impact.rationale: Time-to-power is the stated gating factor for new capacity; grid capex inflecting.

evidence.claim: Utility capex plans raised repeatedly citing data-center load growth.

crowdedness.rationale: Quietest corner of the chain in retail terms; EPC names get episodic attention, utilities almost none as AI plays.

evidence.claim: Grid EPC and utility names rank far below semis in every attention metric.

capture.rationale: THE TRAP EXAMPLE: much of this link is regulated-return or competitively bid EPC — volume without proportional profit capture. Un-crowded partly because capture is capped.

evidence.claim: Regulated utilities earn allowed ROEs regardless of demand strength; EPC margins are bid-competed.

links.name: Energy generation
links.role: The electrons: gas turbines, nuclear (existing fleet + SMR), and firmed renewables contracted to power AI campuses.

bottleneck.note: Gas turbine slots reported sold out years forward; firm power is the scarcest input after land.

impact.rationale: Data-center load growth is the first structural demand increase for US power in two decades; turbine and PPA economics repricing.

evidence.claim: Turbine makers report sold-out delivery slots into the late 2020s; premium PPAs signed by hyperscalers.

crowdedness.rationale: Merchant power and turbine names discovered in 2024-26 waves (IPPs re-rated hard); SMR names episodically feverish; the industrial core less so.

evidence.claim: IPP re-ratings drew coverage; turbine industrials still framed as boring industrials.

capture.rationale: Turbines: concentrated three-player supply with service annuities. Merchant power: capture depends on market structure; SMRs speculative.

evidence.claim: Heavy-duty gas turbine supply is effectively three vendors globally, each with decades-long service tails.

scenarios.title: Capex supercycle persists through 2028
scenarios.narrative: Hyperscaler and sovereign AI capex keeps compounding; the buildout stays supply-constrained upstream. The quiet links (power, generation, cooling) re-rate as their backlogs extend while the chip layer grows into its multiple.

links_moved.why: Backlog extension plus pricing power; the least-owned link with the most direct order flow.
Firm power scarcity monetizes turbine slots and existing fleets.
Density transition sustains attach rates.
Transmission capex inflects, though capture stays mixed.
Each cluster generation refreshes the fabric.

leading_indicators.where_to_watch: electrical equipment maker calls; industry lead-time surveys

invalidation_signs: Two consecutive quarters of hyperscaler capex guide-downs
Transformer lead times normalizing below 12 months

scenarios.title: Power becomes the binding constraint
scenarios.narrative: Chip supply normalizes but electrons do not: interconnection queues, transformer shortages, and turbine slots gate AI deployment. Value migrates from the compute layer to whoever controls time-to-power.

links_moved.why: Queue position becomes the scarce asset.
Shortage pricing on transformers and switchgear.
Behind-the-meter and firm-PPA premiums blow out.
Shipments gated by powered capacity, not demand.
Unpowered shells; slower monetization of pipelines.

leading_indicators.indicator: Interconnection queue wait times and reform progress
leading_indicators.where_to_watch: LBNL queue studies; FERC dockets; utility IRPs

leading_indicators.indicator: Gas turbine and behind-the-meter order books
leading_indicators.where_to_watch: GEV / Siemens Energy / MHI earnings calls

leading_indicators.indicator: WIRING TEST — verifies the automated indicator pipeline; replace with a real level after first trip

invalidation_signs: On-site generation (gas bridge, SMR) scales faster than expected

scenarios.title: Digestion: capex pause in 2027
scenarios.narrative: Model efficiency plus investor pressure produce a hyperscaler capex plateau. Order momentum stalls across the chain; the crowded links de-rate hardest, backlog-rich industrials hold best.

links_moved.why: Highest multiple on the most cyclical line.
Memory cyclicality reasserts.
Attach-rate growth stalls with new halls.
Backlogs cushion but orders slow.
PPA urgency fades; merchant premiums compress.

leading_indicators.indicator: Hyperscaler language shift from growth to efficiency/FCF
GPU lead times and cloud instance spot pricing normalizing

invalidation_signs: Capex guidance keeps rising for two more quarters across the group

scenarios.title: Efficiency shock
scenarios.narrative: An algorithmic or inference breakthrough cuts compute intensity per unit of capability by an order of magnitude. Application economics improve; hardware demand growth resets lower before Jevons effects rebuild it.

links_moved.why: Direct compute-intensity hit at the highest expectations.
Attached to accelerator units.
Grid and replacement demand cushion the AI component.
Cost curve collapse expands app-layer margins and use cases.
Training-scale moat thins.

leading_indicators.indicator: Inference cost per unit capability trajectory
Open-weight model capability jumps vs frontier

invalidation_signs: Efficiency gains absorbed by demand elasticity with capex unchanged (Jevons confirmation)
